newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Micro reports $13 million quarterly profit.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Micro reports $13 million quarterly profit.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. on Monday reported a first-quarter profit, when Wall Street was expecting a loss, on strong sales of its computer chips.

AMD, as the company is generally known, said it had profits of $12.95 million, or 9 cents a share, for the quarter ended March 30, compared with net income of $25.3 million, or 18 cents, in the same quarter a year ago.
Wall Street expected AMD, a maker of specialized memory chips and microprocessors, to report a loss of 3 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates.
First-quarter revenue rose 1.4 percent to $552 million from $544.2 million a year ago. Revenue for the most recent quarter was about $10 million higher than Wall Street expected.

"The important message of the first quarter is that the company is profitable and that they are starting an incredible product cycle," said analyst Mark Edelstone, at brokerage Prudential Securities Inc.
Last week, AMD introduced the K6 chip, a microprocessor for standard personal computers that can handle basic calculations slightly faster than Intel's top-of-the-line Pentium Pro chip.
Based on expected demand for an alternative to Intel's pricey offerings and improving operations, AMD stock has doubled since the beginning of the year.
The results were announced after the market closed Monday. AMD shares had risen $1.875 to $41.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. The shares rose an additional $1.75 to $43 in after-hour trading.

AMD, based in Sunnyvale, Calif., attributed the better-than-expected results to strong sales of all its products, including flash memory chips and the K5 microprocessor, a rival to Intel Corp.'s low-end Pentium chips. Company officials were not immediately available for more comment.
